title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives Election for New Jersey's 7th Congressional District
description: The 2026 general election for New Jersey's 7th Congressional District pits two-term Republican incumbent Thomas Kean Jr. against Democratic nominee Rebecca Bennett, a former U.S. Navy helicopter pilot and healthcare executive. The district covers Hunterdon and Warren counties and parts of Morris, Somerset, Sussex, and Union counties, with a slight Republican voter registration edge. Kean has been absent from Congress since March 2026 due to an undisclosed medical condition, a fact that has become a central campaign issue and has led national analysts to shift the race rating to "Lean R" or "Toss Up." Democrats view this seat as a key pickup opportunity in their effort to flip the narrowly divided U.S. House, while Republicans argue Kean's record of bipartisan work and constituent service merits re-election.

polling.pollster: Z to A Research (314 Action Fund)

polling_note: One poll has been identified from June 2026 showing Bennett leading Kean by 4 points. Additional independent polling may be released as the general election approaches.

candidates.name: Thomas Kean Jr.
candidates.summary: Thomas Kean Jr. is the two-term Republican incumbent representing New Jersey's 7th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. He previously served as New Jersey Senate Minority Leader for 14 years and was the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in 2006. Kean serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee and the Foreign Affairs Committee.

candidates.name: Rebecca Bennett
candidates.summary: Rebecca Bennett is a former U.S. Navy helicopter pilot and experimental test pilot with over a decade of military service, including service in the Air National Guard. She is a healthcare business leader who earned her MBA from the Wharton School and now runs for Congress on a platform of lowering costs, expanding healthcare access, and national security. She won the Democratic primary on June 2, 2026, and has raised over $2.7 million without corporate PAC money.

forecast.rationale: This is a highly competitive race with very sparse data. The only identified poll (June 2026, from a Democratic-aligned source) shows Rebecca Bennett ahead of incumbent Thomas Kean Jr. by 4 points (47%-43%), suggesting genuine vulnerability for the two-term Republican. However, with only one partisan-aligned poll and no independent or GOP polling available, the polling picture is incomplete. The district has a slight Republican voter registration edge, and Kean is an incumbent, but his prolonged absence from Congress since March 2026 due to an undisclosed medical condition is a significant liability that has eroded his incumbency advantage. National analysts have shifted the race to 'Lean R' or 'Toss Up.' Bennett has strong fundraising ($2.7M without corporate PAC money) and a compelling personal story. On balance, the district's underlying Republican tilt gives Kean a narrow edge, but the race is highly uncertain and could easily flip given the sparse data and unusual circumstances.
